draftPackage.topic: The jellyfish that can reverse its life cycle
draftPackage.centralQuestion: How can an adult jellyfish return to a polyp, and what does that mean for immortality?
draftPackage.thesis: An adult medusa can reorganize through a cyst into polyps that bud new medusae; reversible development does not mean death is impossible.

claims.statement: Attached T.dohrnii polyps form colonies and bud new free-swimming medusae, which grow into adults; gametes produce planula larvae that can settle into polyps.

claims.statement: Injury or unfavorable conditions such as starvation can induce medusa-to-polyp reversal.

evidence.locator: Introduction and Methods: starved barcode-confirmed medusae from Panama.

claims.statement: In a supported reversal route the medusa shrinks, loses swimming ability and recognizable medusa structures, settles as a cyst-like mass, and develops stolons and polyps.

evidence.locator: Introduction, Figure1 and cyst morphology.

claims.statement: A stolon can grow from the cyst and develop polyp buds, eventually producing a colony capable of budding new medusae.

evidence.locator: Figure1 and LCR experiment stages.

visualOpportunities.title: Medusa to cyst to colony
visualOpportunities.description: One translucent species-informed adult medusa suspended in a dark teal water column, red-brown central manubrium, fine moving tentacles and grazing light. Immediate large subject and short curiosity statement. Stay with same adult. Camera arcs to reveal transparent bell and four radial canals; species name large enough to read. Original illustration disclosure. Camera descends to attached branching polyps. A pear-shaped medusa bud grows below a hydranth, detaches and rises; continue toward recognizable adult. No ephyra/disc stack. Same adult loses pulse and descends toward substrate; tentacles retract and bell contracts. No clock, reversed footage, shrinking baby or injury gore. Continuous collapse toward a lobed intermediate then compact cyst-like mass on substrate. Bell and tentacles vanish as recognizable structures; time compression disclosed. Camera pushes from surface of cyst into original illustrative tissue field; some elongated cells lose and change shape amongst surviving cells. No specific traced lineage, molecule, DNA repair visualization or literal microscopy. End by pulling toward cyst surface. A stolon visibly extends sideways from cyst. First polyp rises, then branches develop into a colony. A medusa bud subsequently detaches; support survives through sequence. Widen to cultured colony/medusa relationship; restrained ghosted earlier stage chain indicates another possible reversal, not an infinite loop. Laboratory context explicit. Macro colony remains physical; briefly return to illustrative tissue field with varied cell identities. Molecular controls still studied; no identified master switch. Return to ocean scale: fragile medusa remains small against passing out-of-focus predator silhouette and light shadow. No specific predator species or escaping/resurrection performance implied. Beautiful medusa above living attached polyp colony, then camera settles on colony and new bud ascending into light. Resolve initial adult-only mental model through changed developmental route; no infinity or guaranteed survival.

segments.text: What if an animal could reverse its own life cycle?
Normally, attached polyps bud off tiny jellyfish, which grow into swimming adults.
But injury or starvation can send an adult another way.
Its bell collapses. Its tentacles disappear. It settles into a cyst-like mass.
Inside, cells reorganize. Some can change their specialized identity: transdifferentiation.
A stolon grows, then polyps. That colony can bud new jellyfish.
Life-cycle reversal can happen repeatedly in laboratory cultures.
The molecular controls are still being studied.
But predators can still kill it. Reversal isn't guaranteed survival.
It doesn't make death impossible. It makes the direction of development reversible.

misconceptionSafeguards: Adult → cyst → stolon/polyps → colony/new medusa, not adult → baby.
No rewind, clock, immortality shield or inferred endless wild lifespan.
Specialized-cell participation supported; not every cell reprograms. Cell forms explicitly illustrative, not observed lineage tracing.
Molecular networks are candidates, controls still studied; no anti-aging treatment promise.
No ten-repeat count transferred from unidentified species.
T.rubra absence of reported postreproductive reversal is not proof of no reversal ever.
Research-only anatomy references;16-tentacle form not a species-universal count.
Disease incidence not independently established; no claim of disease immunity or quantified causes of death.

review.rightsReview: All original deterministic production code and synthesized sound, existing licensed fonts and local Kokoro. Research texts retained as evidence only, no scientific figures or unlicensed photos in render.
